title: Terminals
description: Shells on this machine that outlive server restarts: the Terminal page, terminal tabs on workspaces, and running a script in a new terminal

settings.label: Shell
settings.description: The program new terminals run, as an absolute path (for example /bin/zsh, /usr/bin/fish, or on Windows C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe). Empty uses your login shell (on Windows PowerShell 7 if installed, else Windows PowerShell). A path that is not an executable file is ignored.

settings.label: Shell arguments
settings.description: Separated by spaces. -l starts a login shell, so your profile and PATH apply (the default); leave empty for a plain shell. On Windows the default -l is dropped unless you chose a shell (PowerShell starts with -NoLogo).

settings.label: Start folder
settings.description: Where terminals in the Terminal tab start (a terminal on a workspace starts in that workspace's folder). An absolute path, or ~/… for your home.

settings.label: Startup command
settings.description: Typed, with Enter, into every new terminal once it is up (not for scripts run from a ▶ Terminal button), for example: tmux new -As main. One line.

settings.label: History to keep (lines)
settings.description: How many lines of history a new terminal keeps and restores. The terminal daemon learns this setting when it is next restarted after an update; shells already open are not changed.

settings.label: Start the terminal daemon with the app
settings.description: Off if you run it yourself (for example under launchd, systemd or Task Scheduler).
